02

TWO PLAYERS
BUILT THEIR
OWN LEAGUE

NAPHEESA
COLLIER

"Phee." UConn. Minnesota Lynx.

The problem

WNBA players used to spend every offseason playing overseas just to make money.

Their fix

So Phee and Breanna Stewart started Unrivaled — a 3-on-3 league here at home, where the players own equity.

September 2025 · after her season ended

Then Phee went after the league
and its commissioner.

Collier's exit interview
@cnn
Open in TikTok ↗
Then they held up signs.
Nneka Ogwumike, president of the players' union, with the bargaining committee
And then they won

Phee, Stewie and Nneka Ogwumike negotiated the most groundbreaking contract in the history of women's pro sports.

A seven-year deal running 2026 through 2032. Here is what changed.

THE NEW DEAL

2025 → 2026
Salary cap (what a whole team can spend)
$1.5M→$7M
Top salary (supermax)
$249K→$1.4M
Average salary
$120K→$583K
League minimum
$66K→$270K

Plus: revenue sharing tied to how much the league actually makes · charter flights and real housing · paid parental leave and fertility benefits

What it means for one player
Caitlin Clark
#1 pick, 2024
$76,535
vs
Azzi Fudd
#1 pick, 2026
$500,000

Same job. Two years apart. A 553% raise.

The part that made everyone cry

They went back and paid the retired players too.

$30K5–7 years played
$50K8–11 years
$100K12+ years

Over $14 million to roughly 280 women who built the league and never got paid for it.

Teammates at UConn
for four years.

They both kept getting hurt. Paige tore her ACL and lost an entire season. Azzi went down with knee injuries of her own, twice.

They took turns being the one on crutches — sitting through each other's surgeries and rehab, and each getting the other through it.

In 2025 they were finally healthy at the same time, and won the national championship.

The Indiana Fever.

SOPHIE
CUNNINGHAM

Got famous for fighting. Not for basketball.

June 2025: another player poked Caitlin Clark in the eye. Sophie grabbed her and threw her out of bounds. Ejected.

She gained nearly a million followers in three days.

Asked to name her favourite rap song

She answered with country music.

Open in TikTok ↗

Can't leave trans people alone

…protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men.
— Sophie Cunningham, in an ESPN profile

Asked about it again, she doubled down: "I said what I said. I think it's kind of common sense."

It set off three separate rallies and a reaction that went all the way to the White House.

CAITLIN
CLARK

Her rookie year, fans were worried she was getting hurt — hard fouls, no whistles. She pushed for tighter officiating, and the league listened: a task force, and new instructions to referees.

Then it backfired. Tighter officiating means more fouls called on everyone, including her — and she argues every one of them.

Seven technical fouls this season, tied with Angel Reese for the most in the league. One more is an automatic suspension, so the Fever keep appealing them.

As the league got popular — thanks to TikTok and a few electric players including Clark — Black players started getting racist attacks from fans, at games and online.

Death threats. Slurs. AI-generated images sent to their families. The list goes on.

The attacks get worse when those players face the Indiana Fever and Caitlin Clark.

The online abuse is thoroughly documented. The one formal in-arena allegation (Gainbridge, May 2025) was investigated by the WNBA and could not be substantiated.
06

COUPLES
AND ROMANTIC
DRAMA

ALYSSA THOMAS
& DEWANNA BONNER

DeWanna was married to another WNBA player through the mid-2010s. She had twins through IVF in 2017, and the couple split after.

She and Alyssa got together as teammates on the Connecticut Sun and got engaged in 2023. Alyssa stepped all the way in with the twins — the dad who stepped up.

In 2025 DeWanna signed with the Indiana Fever. It did not work out; she lasted nine games. Phoenix picked her up — where Alyssa already was.

They have had 30-point games on the same night, as a couple, on the same team.

DIJONAI

DiJonai and NaLyssa met at Baylor and dated for five years.

Last year they played for the Dallas Wings with Paige Bueckers — then got traded to two different teams. People started calling Paige a child of divorce.

DiJonai still cheered NaLyssa on when she won the championship last year.
